assumption: the eviction rate is set by ARRIVALS (COLD rotation admitting newly-observed markets) and is therefore cap-invariant at steady state; residency then scales linearly with the non-protected slot count
finding: evicted_idle is 0 in every sample: NOTHING reaches the 2 h idle rule, so eviction is driven entirely by the cap and the dict is saturated and thrashing
headline: at the CURRENT cap of 1500 the mean unseated market already survives less than the 3600 s that trades_1h needs; every lower cap makes that strictly worse
method: Little's law on steady-state eviction: a dict held at its cap with arrivals equal to evictions gives mean residency = non_protected_slots / eviction_rate
